questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was mainly drawn by the large number of courses relevant to my studies taught in English. Furthermore, I have long wished to visit and explore the destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Both my host university, and the local authorities, was of great assistance with information about my destination, studies, and local regulations.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My host university instructed me in registration with the local authorities and preparations for my studies.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I received a housing offer in a university dormitory through my host university, which was a great help for a smooth start in my city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: My faculty did not have a campus area for student living, so students lived all throughout the city. This is not a problem as public transportation and biking is readily available throughout.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration is handled through a self-service online platform by the university and was fairly intuitive to me. However, I discovered that some courses (courses related to archaeology and ancient studies) are handled manually by university staff and require correspondence with these. This made the process more lengthy and confusing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Staff were available through messaging to answer questions and guide students through registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to get into most of the courses I was interested in, and since the university offered a wide selection of elective courses, I had no problem choosing more than was necessary.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be in good time and ask for help in case of any confusion.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My courses were varied, but were all interesting and challenging. I thought they were all suitable for my level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Some courses were more heavy on lectures in large groups than I am used to. Other courses followed a largely class-based discussion style as is more used at UCPH.
I was surprised at the amount of obligatory written assignments during each course, which differed greatly from my prior experiences. The final gradings of the courses were also typically dependent on the outcome of different assignments handed in during the course as well as a final exam at the end of the course, which is very different to the style at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Archaeology and Society, Ancient Philosophy, Spain: Mediterranean Microcosm of Europe, Nation building and nation branding in postcolonial states, and Classical Mythology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I especially enjoyed the following courses.
Spain: Mediterranean Microcosm of Europe, Nation building and nation branding in postcolonial states, and Classical Mythology.
I would not recommend Archaeology and Society to anybody else than archaeologists. As a historian, the course was unfortunately not as relevant to me, as I had hoped.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I choose to rent a bike for ca. 200 kr. a month instead of using mostly public transportation. On the other hand, internet and utilities were included in my rent. However, laundry and food was on the more expensive side.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Laundry and food was on the more expensive side, as is public transport if you choose to exclusively use that. As a Dane, I suggest buying or renting a bike while in Amsterdam.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many parties, social activities such as film nights, visits to museums, breweries etc. and the like arranged by student groups (like the Erasmus Student Network) outside of the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try to participate in the Erasmus Student Network's activities at the beginning of the semester, this is an opportunity to meet many other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city, Amsterdam has much to offer in terms of culture and experiences. I liked their museums, parks and walks through the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The Netherlands is in many ways much like Copenhagen in terms of culture and geography. Therefore, I found it quite manageable.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Everyone speaks English, and I found many local students as well as exchange students in my classes. I regularly spoke with a few local students when in class, but otherwise not so much.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone was lovely and kind to me, and I experienced a very understanding and loose culture, where everyone wanted to see you succeed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The university's staff is extremely helpful with any problems you might encounter, so do not hesitate with contacting them for help.
I strongly recommend getting a bike for transportation; it is both cheeper, more environmentally friendly, good for you, and gives you the greatest freedom to experience the city. The metro is excellent as well, but it is difficult to really see and feel the city, when you are mostly in a tube underground.
Try to meet some people and make some friends in the beginning of your stay, as it gets harder once the academic year really picks up.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: University housing is only available to around 50% of all exchange students, and renting privately can be difficult, time-consuming and expensive. Be proactive and willing to spend some money when it comes to securing university housing, as short-term renting in Amsterdam can be a challenge.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned so much! Both academically and personally. I especially appreciate the opportunity to branch out in many different elective courses with different styles of teaching.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Homesickness. I missed my friends and family at home, but Amsterdam is not much more than an hour away by plane, and visits from home as well as frequent calls was a massive advantage for me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
